business_model.claim: Pebblebrook is an internally managed hotel REIT. It owns hotels mainly in major U.S. cities and nearby or destination resort markets, with an emphasis on gateway coastal markets.
quotes: Pebblebrook Hotel Trust is an internally managed hotel investment company, formed as a Maryland real estate investment trust in October 2009 to opportunistically acquire and invest in hotel properties located primarily in major United States cities and resort properties located near our primary target urban markets and select destination resort markets, with an emphasis on major gateway coastal markets.

business_model.claim: The portfolio was 44 hotels with 11,052 guest rooms at December 31, 2025. After the Hotel Zags sale it was 42 hotels with approximately 10,800 rooms across 14 markets.
quotes: As of December 31, 2025, the Company owned interests in 44 hotels with a total of 11,052 guest rooms.
The Company owns 42 hotels, totaling approximately 10,800 guest rooms across 14 urban and resort markets.

business_model.claim: The company does not run its hotels itself. REIT rules bar it from operating them, so the hotels are leased to a taxable REIT subsidiary (PHL), which hires third-party managers. PHL is consolidated, so hotel-level revenue and costs appear in the company's statements.
quotes: For the Company to maintain its qualification as a REIT under the Code, it cannot operate the hotels it owns.
PHL is consolidated into the Company's financial statements.

business_model.claim: The company sells hotel stays and related services to business transient, leisure transient, and group and convention guests.
quotes: We believe that portfolio diversification will allow us to benefit from growth in various customer categories, including business transient, leisure transient and group and convention room-night demand.

business_model.claim: Revenue has three streams. Q3 2026 total revenues were 402,745 (table in thousands): room 258,253, food and beverage 96,252 and other operating 48,240. Nine-month 2026 totals were 1,155,543, made up of room 732,491, food and beverage 289,969 and other operating 133,083.

business_model.basis: stated in P4 table; P3 names these metrics as key indicators
business_model.claim: Room revenue depends on occupancy and average daily rate (ADR), which together give RevPAR (revenue per available room). Q3 2026 same-property occupancy was 80.6% against 79.6%, ADR was $318.52 against $297.56, and RevPAR was $256.66 against $236.96.
Q3 2026 growth was led by room rates more than occupancy: same-property RevPAR rose 8.3%, ADR rose 7.0% and occupancy rose 1.2%.
quotes: Same-Property RevPAR +8.3%, driven by ADR +7.0% and Occupancy +1.2%

business_model.claim: Guest spending outside the room matters most at the resorts. In Q3 2026 resort RevPAR rose 8.4% and resort food and beverage revenues rose 11.2%.
quotes: Resort RevPAR increased 8.4%, food and beverage revenues jumped 11.2%, and eight of our 13 resorts achieved Hotel EBITDA growth of 20% or more.

business_model.claim: Revenue is moved by demand in specific markets and by events. Q3 2026 RevPAR rose 14.5% in San Francisco and 12.7% in Chicago. Management cited the World Cup and America 250 events, and says limited new hotel supply supports pricing.
quotes: With new hotel supply extremely limited, stronger pricing power and disciplined cost control are driving higher RevPAR, total revenues, and margins.

business_model.claim: Revenue is seasonal: the first and fourth quarters are weaker and the second and third quarters are stronger.
quotes: Generally, our hotels have lower revenue, operating income and cash flow in the first and fourth quarters of each year and higher revenue, operating income and cash flow in the second and third quarters of each year.

business_model.claim: Hotel operating expenses are the largest cost. They were 256,719 of 430,363 total operating expenses in Q3 2026 (table in thousands). The parts were room 68,344, food and beverage 70,632 and other operating 117,743.
The cost drivers the company names are wages and benefits, repair and maintenance, property taxes and insurance. Rising wages and benefits added to 2025 hotel operating expenses.
quotes: wage and benefit costs, which may include an increase in minimum wages and health benefit costs; repair and maintenance expenses; property taxes; insurance costs; and other operating expenses
as well as an increase in wages and benefits throughout most of our portfolio

business_model.claim: High fixed costs give operating leverage. In Q3 2026 same-property total revenues rose 6.9% while total expenses rose 4.0%. Weak demand would work in reverse and hurt profitability.

In addition, in periods of weak demand, as may occur during a general economic recession, profitability is adversely affected by the relatively high fixed costs of operating upper-upscale hotels and resorts.
